easy.explanation: The verse begins, “Then said the LORD unto me.”
easy.q: Who told Hosea to love a woman?

easy.explanation: The LORD told Hosea to love a woman who was “an adulteress.”
The verse says that they “look to other gods.”
easy.q: Whom did the children of Israel look to?

answers: The love of the LORD toward Israel
medium.explanation: The verse compares Hosea’s love with “the love of the LORD toward the children of Israel.”
medium.q: What did Hosea’s love for the woman represent?

medium.explanation: The verse says they “love flagons of wine.”
medium.q: What did the Israelites love in addition to other gods?

medium.explanation: An adulteress is an unfaithful woman.
medium.q: What does “adulteress” mean in this context?

challenge.explanation: The woman is called an adulteress, while Israel looks to other gods.
challenge.q: What common condition connects the woman and Israel?

answers: Love that begins only after repentance
challenge.explanation: Hosea is commanded to love an unfaithful woman, portraying the LORD’s love for Israel.
challenge.q: What does the comparison between Hosea’s love and the LORD’s love emphasize?

answers: Between a king and a prince
challenge.explanation: The command to love stands beside the woman’s unfaithfulness and Israel’s turning to other gods.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in the verse?

paragraphs.title: Acquiring the Woman and Establishing the Bond

easy.explanation: Hosea bought her with silver and barley.
easy.q: What did Hosea give for the woman?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “fifteen pieces of silver.”
easy.q: How many pieces of silver did Hosea pay?

easy.explanation: Hosea said, “Thou shalt abide for me many days.”
easy.q: What did Hosea tell the woman to do?

medium.explanation: The payment included fifteen pieces of silver and measured quantities of barley.
Hosea first bought the woman, and then gave her instructions about waiting.
medium.q: What happened first in these verses?

answers: I gave her a new name
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Hosea’s act of acquiring the woman.
medium.q: What does “I bought her to me” mean?

answers: She will not be another man’s, and Hosea will also be hers
She will leave Hosea, and he will marry another
They will both seek other gods
challenge.explanation: She must not be for another man, and Hosea says, “so will I also be for thee.”

answers: A period of waiting and faithfulness
challenge.explanation: Remaining alone reflects the waiting and exclusive commitment required in the passage.
challenge.q: What does her abiding alone suggest?

answers: The purchase is followed by a commitment to wait faithfully
The purchase ends all contact between them
The purchase requires her to follow other gods
challenge.explanation: After buying her, Hosea establishes a period in which neither belongs to another.
challenge.q: How are the purchase and Hosea’s instructions related?

paragraphs.title: The Period of Waiting and Absence of Leadership

easy.explanation: The verse says they will be “without a king, and without a prince.”
easy.q: What will the children of Israel be without?

answers: A sacrifice, an image, an ephod, and teraphim
easy.explanation: The verse lists a sacrifice, an image, an ephod, and teraphim.
easy.q: Which religious objects are also mentioned as absent?

answers: Israel’s period without leadership and religious symbols
The king’s life in his palace
easy.explanation: Her waiting corresponds to Israel’s long period without a king, ruler, sacrifice, or listed religious objects.
easy.q: What does the woman’s waiting symbolize?

answers: Both describe a lack of leadership or religious practice
medium.explanation: The verse combines political absence with the absence of religious observances and objects.
medium.q: What do the absence of a king and the absence of sacrifice have in common?

medium.explanation: In this list, the ephod is a religious object associated with worship.
medium.q: In the KJV, what is an “ephod”?

answers: Both involve a long period without normal leadership and religious symbols
medium.explanation: The verse describes Israel abiding many days without its king, prince, sacrifice, image, ephod, or teraphim.
medium.q: Why does the period of waiting fit the picture of Israel?

answers: Waiting, absence of leadership, and absence of religious symbols
challenge.explanation: Israel will abide many days without political leadership and several religious objects or practices.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in the verse?

answers: A king, a prince, a sacrifice, an image, an ephod, and teraphim
challenge.explanation: These are the specific things listed in the verse.
challenge.q: What does the verse explicitly say Israel will be without?

challenge.explanation: The phrase plainly describes a time without a king or ruling prince.
challenge.q: What does “without a king, and without a prince” signify?

paragraphs.title: Return and Seeking the Lord at the End of Days

answers: The LORD their God and David their king
easy.explanation: The verse says they will seek “the LORD their God, and David their king.”
easy.q: Whom will the children of Israel seek?

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “Afterward shall the children of Israel return.”
easy.q: What will the children of Israel do afterward?

answers: At the beginning of the days
During the middle of the kingdom
easy.explanation: The verse ends with “in the latter days.”

answers: They return, seek the LORD and David, and fear the LORD and his goodness
They choose a king, go into exile, and then return
They seek other gods and then depart
medium.explanation: The verse describes returning, seeking, and fearing the LORD and his goodness.
medium.q: What is the order of events in the verse?
Whom do they seek together with the LORD?

answers: The beginning of the waiting period
The day Hosea bought the woman
medium.explanation: The expression refers to a later or concluding time.

answers: Israel returns and seeks the LORD
Israel turns again to other gods
challenge.explanation: After the period without leadership and religious symbols, Israel will return and seek the LORD.
challenge.q: What change follows the period described in the previous verse?

answers: From looking to other gods to seeking the LORD
From loving the LORD to rejecting him
challenge.explanation: Earlier Israel looked to other gods; here they seek the LORD their God.
challenge.q: What change in Israel’s direction is described?

answers: Reverence and longing for the LORD and his goodness
A desire to worship other gods
challenge.explanation: Their fear is a reverent response to the LORD and to his goodness.
challenge.q: What does fearing the LORD and his goodness express?
